links.outcome: Gemini accuracy interpreting ovarian ultrasound (O-RADS/IOTA) vs histopathology, rated by GQS
links.effect: Mean GQS 3; 6/10 normal ovaries mischaracterized as pathologic; 6/10 benign lesions assigned O-RADS 4-5; 3/10 malignant misclassified as benign (O-RADS 2), plus 1 borderline tumor misclassified.
links.quote: Critical inconsistencies including overdiagnosis and dangerous misclassification of malignancies indicate the need for specialized, domain-specific models with rigorous validation before clinical implementation.

links.outcome: Risk of missed or incorrect diagnoses if the AI output were used as stand-alone diagnosis
links.effect: Gemini misclassified 3/10 malignant cases as benign (O-RADS 2, GQS 1) and overdiagnosed 6/10 normal ovaries as pathologic; authors conclude it is not ready for independent clinical application.
links.quote: Google Gemini seems to not be ready for independent clinical application in ovarian ultrasound interpretation.

screen.reason: Retrospective diagnostic benchmark evaluating Google Gemini's ability to interpret ovarian ultrasound images using O-RADS and IOTA criteria compared to expert and histopathology standards.
